newsitem.title: GREECE: Olympic Airways is back in profit after 19 years in the red.
newsitem.headline: Olympic Airways is back in profit after 19 years in the red.

text.p: Greece's state carrier Olympic Airways was back in the black, registering a profit of about 9.9 billion drachmas ($40.4 million) in fiscal 1995 after 19 years of losses, it said in a statement on Wednesday.

"After 19 years of registering losses, the 1995 fiscal year was a profit-making one for Olympic Airways with the company showing a high cash balance and a real profit of some 9.9 billion drachmas," it said.

"It is too early for 1996 results because the year is not over yet," said Annie Manta, chief public relations officer when asked to clarify whether there were any results for 1996. "The 1996 results will be out at the end of 1997. This is what most companies do with their results."
The company's statement of accounts for 1995 was approved by its board of directors on September 17 1996, it said.
The operating profits stood at 13.3 billion drachmas in 1995 and cash liquidity increased to 49.7 billion drachmas at the end of 1995 compared to 21.5 billion in 1994, it said.
"The company's aims continue to focus on full implementation of the restructuring plan approved by the EU Commission on October 7, 1994 and the Greek government on December 14, 1994," it said.

European Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock, speaking at a news conference in Brussels, welcomed the result but warned that Commission inquiries into Olympic's restructuring plan remained unresolved.
"There are some outstanding matters, and one very specific concern, that will have to be resolved. The Greek authorities understand that very well," Kinnock said, without giving further detail.

The European Commission expressed serious doubts about the restructuring package in an official notice published in July, saying the Greek government had failed to meet various commitments made in respect of the 54-billion-drachma package of loan guarantees, debt write-offs and debt-to-equity conversions. ($ = 245.0 Greek Drachmas)
